title: Leader Election: Complete Architecture
description: Design a leader election service using distributed consensus with ephemeral locks and fencing to avoid split-brain.

data.text: Design a leader election mechanism so exactly one node in a distributed system performs the role of coordinator (e.g. scheduler, lock manager, or partition leader). The system must detect failures within seconds, elect a new leader safely, and never have two leaders active simultaneously.

terms.definition: Two nodes both believe they are leader, which can cause data corruption if both write to the same resource.
A node in a consensus store that is automatically removed if its session expires. This makes a crashed leader's claim disappear without cleanup.
If the leader fails to send heartbeats before its session expires, its ephemeral lease disappears and another candidate can take over.
Minimising the time between a leader crash and a new leader taking over, while still ensuring safety.
A time-bounded claim that the leader must renew; if not renewed, it lapses automatically.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Exactly-One Leader: safety — at any moment there is 0 or 1 leader, never 2
Automatic Failover: elect a new leader when the current one crashes or becomes unreachable
Leadership Renewal: the leader must heartbeat periodically to keep its claim
Leader Discovery: all nodes can discover who the current leader is
Clean Handoff: a leader should relinquish leadership on shutdown

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: Failover Time: under 5 seconds to detect and elect a new leader
Correctness: no split-brain under network partitions
Low Overhead: heartbeats every 1 second at most

data.caption: Leader Election: Candidates compete for an ephemeral lock in a consensus store; clients discover the leader via a registry
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    C1[Candidate A]
    C2[Candidate B]
    C3[Candidate C]
    Store[(Raft/etcd with ephemeral nodes)]
    Clients[Service Clients]

    C1 -->|Create ephemeral /leader| Store
    C2 -->|Try to create /leader| Store
    C3 -->|Watch /leader| Store
    Store -->|Leader identity| C3
    C1 -.->|Heartbeat lease| Store
    Clients -->|Discover leader| Store

data.text: Use a consensus-backed ephemeral key. The first node to successfully create the key becomes leader. The key has a TTL/lease and the leader must renew it; if it fails to renew, the key is deleted automatically and another candidate claims it.

data.title: Leader election with etcd-like lease
Key Takeaways
points: Ephemeral leases plus renewal prevent split-brain automatically
Safety comes from the consensus store's linearizable writes
Watchers enable fast discovery of leadership changes
Failover time is determined by lease expiry and election latency
data.takeaway: Consensus-backed ephemeral locks are the simplest and safest way to implement leader election.
